title: Potsdam Conference
summary: Allied leaders of the United States, Britain and the Soviet Union met at Potsdam, near Berlin, to settle the administration of defeated Germany, Poland's boundaries and the war against Japan. They issued an ultimatum demanding Japan's unconditional surrender. Disagreements were largely postponed to a Council of Foreign Ministers, and it was the last Allied summit.

where.modern_name: Potsdam, Germany (Schloss Cecilienhof), a suburb of Berlin

importance.justification: Shaped postwar occupation of Germany, Poland's borders and the ultimatum to Japan, ahead of the Cold War division.
